title: How Does Leverage Affect Trading Returns? The Kelly Criterion | Coffeezilla Follow-up
summary: Finance lecturer on leverage and the Kelly criterion: retail traders face professionals, free trading is not free, over-betting wipes out even a real edge, two-percent-a-day promises are absurd.

assertions.quote: most of the people that you are trading against are full-time traders and they're very smart
you should be aware that the majority of day traders do lose money
If you think you're trading for free, you're not trading for free. They're just getting it out of you a different way.
options have significantly higher commissions or trading costs, wider spreads than stocks do

verdicts.note: Options spreads are wider as a percentage of price and liquidity is thinner.

assertions.quote: 28% of the participants went bust, so they lost everything and received no payout

verdicts.note: The Haghani and Dewey biased-coin experiment found a large share of educated participants went bust.

assertions.quote: The most obvious and important one is that excess leverage will definitely wipe you out.
a day trader should not reasonably expect to make more than those investors over any long period of time

verdicts.note: Top long-run track records cluster near twenty percent annualized; retail averages are far below.

assertions.quote: that small sounding daily return compounds out to I had to do the calculation 137,640%
